editions.label: Sunday, 8 November 2026
editions.note: A quieter weekend for product releases, with fresh NSW reporting and significant overseas developments. All publication times below are Sydney time. Preliminary results and company plans are labelled.

stories.title: Psychiatrist calls for clinical control of prison mental health
stories.summary: Leading forensic psychiatrist Kerri Eagle says Justice Health, rather than prison officers, should lead the management of mentally ill NSW inmates. Her intervention follows an ABC investigation identifying dozens of coronial findings about failures in care since 2015.
stories.detail: Eagle is a Justice Health clinical director but spoke in a private capacity, so this is a reform proposal, not an announced government policy. Prison officers currently develop immediate support plans covering housing and observation for inmates in crisis. Corrective Services NSW says progress requires a coordinated, whole-of-government response. The central question is who holds clinical responsibility when an inmate needs urgent care.

stories.title: NSW weighs stronger controls on collision and slap sports
stories.summary: A parliamentary inquiry is examining whether collision-running, competitive slapping and bare-knuckle boxing should be formally classified as combat sports. Friday's hearing exposed a sharp split: the Combat Sports Authority wants stronger controls, while neurologist Rowena Mobbs urged a ban because of brain-injury risks.
stories.detail: Bare Knuckle Australia representatives said they were willing to collaborate on regulation, although organisers differed over how much intervention was appropriate. Collision-running and power-slap organisers did not appear. The inquiry's report is expected by Christmas, so no new rules have been adopted through this process yet. The immediate significance is the direction of NSW event regulation, not a change to ordinary community sport.

stories.title: Newcastle hosts a wet World Cup breakthrough for the Kiwis
stories.summary: New Zealand beat Tonga 34-10 in the Rugby League World Cup semi-final at Hunter Stadium in Newcastle. Kalyn Ponga returned from a broken arm to deliver a man-of-the-match performance in appalling weather.
stories.detail: The result sends the Kiwis into the final. ABC's match analysis credits their pressure and composure in the difficult conditions.

stories.title: No significant fresh Apple development verified
stories.summary: No significant Apple announcement or substantive new development was verified within the past 24 hours. Fresh accessory coverage, shopping offers and weekly recaps do not warrant padding out today's section.
stories.detail: The source link opens MacRumors' dated November archive.

stories.title: Tesla plans an extra Cybertruck shift before the line closes
stories.summary: The substantive update to yesterday's wind-down news: Elon Musk says Tesla will add a production shift to try to clear Cybertruck orders before dismantling the line around June or July 2027. The space is intended for expanded Cybercab production.
stories.detail: Musk says the backlog exceeds what Tesla can currently build before that deadline. This is a production plan, not confirmation that every order will be fulfilled. No change to Australian Model Y servicing, software or charging is confirmed by this announcement.

stories.title: A quiet day for verified AI releases
stories.summary: No significant new AI product release with verified availability was found in the past 24 hours. Recent releases already covered are not being recycled as new meeting, presentation or workflow tools.
stories.detail: The source link is OpenAI's official news index, checked alongside other major providers. No new Australian rollout is claimed today.

stories.title: Who Gives A Crap warns customers after marketing-provider breach
stories.summary: Who Gives A Crap notified customers on Saturday that an unnamed US marketing-software provider had suffered unauthorised access affecting Australian, UK and US customer data. Names, contact information, mailing addresses and total spend were involved, but the company says payment details, order details and passwords were not.
stories.detail: Access began on 30 October and was secured on 1 November; WGAC says it was informed on Friday. It does not yet know whether data was copied or downloaded and reports no evidence of misuse. It has disconnected the provider and changed credentials. My suggested CSM takeaway: use this as a prompt to review third-party access scope and incident-notification responsibilities with relevant teams. The reporting does not identify the vendor, so there is no basis to attribute it to Braze.

stories.title: New Zealand's election is too close to settle
stories.summary: With results from all voting places, National has 29.37 per cent of the party vote against Labour's 29.22 per cent. The National, ACT and NZ First bloc is provisionally projected to hold 67 of 131 seats, only one above the majority threshold.
stories.detail: About 700,000 special votes, including overseas ballots, remain to be processed. That means yesterday's voting has not produced a confirmed government, and both major-party leaders acknowledge negotiations lie ahead. Smaller parties and the final size of parliament could change the balance. Expect weeks of counting and coalition discussions, not a settled winner this weekend.

stories.title: Russian strikes damage Kyiv's energy supply and a major bridge
stories.summary: The attacks Ukraine warned about yesterday have now hit energy infrastructure around Kyiv, with authorities reporting serious pressure on electricity, water and heating as temperatures approach freezing. Missiles also damaged the Northern Bridge across the Dnipro.
stories.detail: Authorities reported at least two deaths and around a dozen injuries across Ukraine. The strikes come before US-brokered Russia-Ukraine talks scheduled in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November. This is a material escalation from the earlier warning, not a repeat of it.

stories.title: Eisenkot gets the first chance to form Israel's government
stories.summary: President Isaac Herzog has selected Benjamin Netanyahu's leading rival, Gadi Eisenkot, to try to assemble a coalition after Israel's deadlocked election. This does not make Eisenkot prime minister: he still needs a parliamentary majority.
stories.detail: The formal offer is expected later on Sunday in Israel, early Monday in Sydney, after which he will initially have 28 days. Arab-Israeli parties hold a record 19 seats and are central to the negotiations. Without their support, Eisenkot would need ultra-Orthodox parties from Netanyahu's previous coalition to change sides. The political outcome remains unresolved.

stories.title: Six killed in Krakow market-square shooting
stories.summary: Polish authorities say six people were killed and 16 injured in a shooting in Krakow's main market square. Police shot the suspected lone attacker, who remains in hospital, and say the public is now safe.
stories.detail: The interior minister says early findings point to far-right ideological influences, but the motive has not been established. One injured police officer is in a critical condition. Treat the ideological assessment and other early details as provisional while investigators establish what happened.

editions.label: Saturday, 7 November 2026
editions.note: Checked Saturday morning, Sydney time. Regional availability, preliminary findings and suggested applications are labelled.

stories.title: Bondi attack survivor Eva Geller dies
stories.summary: Eva Geller, 90, has died after being shot at the Bondi Chanukah gathering last December. ABC reports she was a Holocaust survivor who came to Australia from Hungary as a child and spent much of the past year in hospital or rehabilitation.
stories.detail: NSW Police say they are working with the coroner and awaiting further advice. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and NSW Premier Chris Minns paid tribute to Geller and offered condolences to her family and Sydney's Jewish community.

stories.title: Powerhouse Parramatta opens to the public today
stories.summary: Western Sydney's $915 million museum opens on Saturday with more than 3,000 objects and five major exhibitions. This is the public opening itself, following earlier previews of the works inside.
stories.detail: Entry and four of the five exhibitions are free. The ticketed space and aviation exhibition is $30 for adults, $20 for concessions and free for under-16s. Street parking is limited, so public transport is worth considering if you're heading over from Epping.

stories.title: AFP searches Tokyo flight after Sydney Airport threat
stories.summary: Armed federal police met passengers on an All Nippon Airways flight from Tokyo at Sydney Airport on Thursday night and carried out precautionary searches. A passenger told ABC people were kept on board for about 90 minutes before disembarking.
stories.detail: The AFP confirmed threats had been sent to an airport. Nearly 30 flights were disrupted by separate bomb threats across Europe on Thursday, but authorities have not established a link to Sydney, and no explosives were reported found on the aircraft searched.

stories.title: Apple Australia extends eligible online holiday returns
stories.summary: Eligible items received from Apple Australia's online store between 6 November and 25 December can be returned until 8 January 2027. The window is based on when you receive the item, not simply when you order it.
stories.detail: That gives you more time to decide on a gift or a new device bought directly from Apple. Other retailers have their own policies, and Apple excludes iPhones bought through carrier financing or carrier offers from the extension.

stories.title: Tesla plans to wind down Cybertruck production in Texas
stories.summary: Elon Musk says Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Austin-area factory around mid-2027 to make room for more Cybercabs. AP cites Kelley Blue Book estimates of about 20,200 Cybertruck sales in 2025 and a further 28 per cent fall through September this year.
stories.detail: It is a production plan, not an immediate stop or an Australian robotaxi rollout. The announcement does not confirm a change to Australian Model Y production, support or driver-assistance features.

stories.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small through Tinker
stories.summary: Thinking Machines Lab has made its new vision and reasoning model available in Tinker Playground and for fine-tuning and inference through Tinker. Downloadable weights are planned under Apache 2.0 after external safety testing, but they are not available yet; the announcement does not specify Australian account eligibility.
stories.detail: The lab demonstrated the model using visual feedback to refine interactive websites. My suggested test, if you have access: give it a screenshot of a mock customer review deck and ask it to flag slides where the takeaway is unclear, using dummy data rather than customer material.
stories.published: 5 Nov, vendor date; rollout reported 6 Nov AEDT

stories.title: EU says TikTok's For You feed may breach digital rules
stories.summary: The European Commission says TikTok has not adequately assessed or mitigated the risk of its feed repeatedly steering people towards similar material, including videos about body image or isolation. Regulators want changes to the recommender and easier controls for users to influence what they see.
stories.detail: These are preliminary findings under the Digital Services Act, not a final ruling. TikTok disputes the findings. Any resulting redesign could be worth watching in Australia, but no Australian product change was announced.

stories.title: Canberra presses ahead with defence property sales
stories.summary: The federal government is sticking with its plan to sell 67 Defence properties despite a parliamentary inquiry recommending a halt. ABC reports the sales are expected to bring in about $3 billion gross, or roughly $1.8 billion after remediation costs.
stories.detail: Sydney's Victoria Barracks is on the list, and both of Tasmania's live-fire training areas are earmarked for sale. The government argues that Defence should shift resources north and west, but it has yet to spell out how it will replace the Tasmanian training capacity.

stories.title: New Zealand votes in a tight general election
stories.summary: Polls are open today in New Zealand, where Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National Party and Christopher Hipkins's Labour Party are competing to lead the next government. Cost of living, housing affordability and sluggish growth have dominated the campaign.
stories.detail: Voting closes at 7 pm New Zealand time, or 5 pm in Sydney, with preliminary results released progressively afterwards. Those are not the final numbers: the official count, which includes special and overseas votes, is due on 27 November.

stories.title: Ukraine warns of fresh strikes on critical infrastructure
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukrainian intelligence indicates Russia is preparing new strikes on energy facilities, bridges and other infrastructure. He said the military was preparing for a difficult period.
stories.detail: The warning points to the risk of further disruption to essential services as winter approaches. It is an intelligence assessment reported by Ukraine's president, not confirmation that the anticipated strikes have already happened.

editions.label: Friday, 6 November 2026
editions.note: Checked Friday morning, Sydney time. Stories are deduplicated by underlying event. Releases, beta access, regional availability and suggested applications are labelled explicitly.

stories.title: NSW inquiry says data centre checks miss cumulative pressure
stories.summary: A cross-party NSW inquiry found planning assesses data centres largely as individual projects, missing their combined demands on electricity, water and infrastructure. Current guidance may underestimate future demand and the pressure created when facilities cluster.
stories.detail: The committee stopped short of a moratorium after members voted 6 to 1 to remove that recommendation. It instead called for a state strategy and better coordination across approvals. The issue is especially relevant around Sydney, where residents have opposed projects and major proposals remain under assessment.

stories.title: Sydney Mardi Gras party will return in 2027
stories.summary: The official post-parade party is coming back on 6 March beneath Sydney Football Stadium after this year's event was cancelled weeks before the parade. Organisers say the 2026 party would have cost about $2 million after running at a deficit since 2020.
stories.detail: The wider festival runs from 12 February to 7 March, one week longer than before. The performer line-up is due next Tuesday, member tickets open on 9 November and general and party pre-sales follow on 12 November.

stories.title: Apple Creator Studio's AI update is now rolling out
stories.summary: Apple has started releasing the Creator Studio update announced last month. It brings Generate Fill to Pixelmator Pro, a beta assistant and improved Stem Splitter to Logic Pro, plus context-aware beta assistants and MCP workflow support in Keynote, Pages and Numbers.
stories.detail: Final Cut Pro also gains built-in MotionVFX assets, a Content Hub and smoother Pixelmator Pro editing. The update is free for existing subscribers, but several AI features remain beta. Australian language or regional availability is not confirmed for every assistant, so check the app release notes before relying on them.

stories.title: First touchscreen MacBook Pro reviews are in
stories.summary: Early reviews praise the PROLED XDR tandem OLED display, slimmer design and lower weight, while treating touch as useful rather than transformative. Reviewers found gestures handy for photo work and media controls, but the laptop still behaves primarily like a conventional Mac.
stories.detail: Other changes include a Dynamic Island, redesigned cooling, up to 16TB of storage and revised speakers. The 14-inch and 16-inch models launch in Australia today from A$4,599 and A$5,499 respectively. For a recent MacBook Pro owner, the display and touch experience are the clearest reasons to upgrade.

stories.title: Model Y helps EVs outsell petrol for a third month
stories.summary: Battery electric vehicles took 23.1 per cent of Australia's new vehicle market in October and again outsold petrol-only cars. Tesla's Model Y and BYD's Sealion 7 were among the leading models, showing that electric SUVs are now driving a broad market shift rather than a niche surge.
stories.detail: This is Australian sales context, not a new Tesla feature, software release or change for an existing Model Y. It may strengthen the case for faster charging and service investment, but no owner-facing expansion was announced. No more significant worldwide Tesla product, autonomy, energy or regulatory development was verified in the past 24 hours.

stories.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber to a limited defender group
stories.summary: GPT-6 Cyber is a specialised model for finding, validating and helping patch exploitable software flaws while staying within authorised scope. OpenAI says it found 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities and helped develop working exploits for 948 Linux kernel issues, alongside candidate fixes.
stories.detail: The model is initially available only through the API and Codex to selected approved Daybreak Red customers, with broader Daybreak access planned. It is not a general ChatGPT release and no Australian availability is promised. For customer success work, the practical near-term implication is better automated security review by specialist teams, not a new everyday meeting or follow-up feature.

stories.title: Box announces a plain-language AI workflow builder
stories.summary: Box Architect will let teams describe a business process in ordinary language and turn it into an automated workflow. A related Nvidia-powered retrieval engine is intended to improve answers from company files while reducing token use and response time.
stories.detail: Architect is due to begin beta rollout this quarter for Enterprise Advanced customers, while Context Retrieval is slated for general availability in early 2027. No specific Australian launch was stated. Suggested experiment: describe a transcript-to-follow-up flow that extracts decisions, owners and risks, then drafts a customer email for review. That is my suggested use, not a reported Box deployment.

stories.title: AI accelerates both hacking and the race to patch
stories.summary: Nearly 37,000 software vulnerabilities were reported in the third quarter, triple the year-earlier level, as companies face faster and more sophisticated attacks. Reuters found firms are deploying AI monitoring and patching tools because exploitation can begin within hours of a flaw becoming public.
stories.detail: Recent cases include hacked European supermarket refrigeration systems and the record Binance theft. A security answer can date quickly, so ask vendors about patch speed, monitoring and incident response, not just certifications. This is an industry trend, separate from today's GPT-6 Cyber release.

stories.title: David Jones enters administration after months of payment strain
stories.summary: The 188-year-old department store entered voluntary administration on Thursday, while suppliers told ABC they had waited months for invoices and struggled to get calls answered. Its 38 stores will keep trading while administrators and receivers review the business.
stories.detail: McGrathNicol and FTI Consulting are examining options, with a creditors' meeting due next week. The immediate effect is uncertainty for suppliers, staff and gift-card holders rather than an announced shutdown. The collapse is a significant warning about pressure on discretionary retail before Christmas.

stories.title: Three more tankers are damaged in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran says three more tankers were damaged on Thursday, taking the number of vessel incidents reported since Sunday to at least five. The attacks keep a critical shipping route under pressure as the United States and Iran remain far apart on ending the Gulf conflict.
stories.detail: Qatari mediators say both sides are reviewing proposals, but no breakthrough has been announced on the strait, sanctions, the blockade or Iran's nuclear programme. Oil prices have fallen sharply as traders reassess the likelihood of renewed US strikes after the midterm result, though shipping risk remains high.

stories.title: Russell Brand is found guilty of rape and sexual assault
stories.summary: A London jury found the British comedian and actor guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two other rape charges and one attempted indecent assault charge after an eight-and-a-half-hour deliberation.
stories.detail: The judge revoked Brand's bail and said a significant custodial sentence was inevitable. He has been remanded in custody and will be sentenced on Monday. UK police say they are also investigating rape allegations made by two other women.

editions.label: Thursday, 5 November 2026
editions.note: Checked Thursday morning, Sydney time. Stories are deduplicated by event. Beta software, regional limits, regulatory claims and suggested applications are labelled.

stories.title: Police investigate a major NSW Health cyber breach
stories.summary: About 4GB of data was stolen from an isolated server for NSW Health's Oral Health Fee For Service Scheme. Police say sensitive identification details belonging to a small number of third-party dental providers may be affected.
stories.detail: Officials say no patient information was compromised, no clinical services are at risk and no other NSW agencies were affected. The Cybercrime Squad is leading the investigation and says the apparent perpetrators are outside Australia. The website was taken offline after the intrusion was detected on 29 October.

stories.title: Powerhouse Parramatta restores an overlooked Dharug botanical story
stories.summary: A rooftop artwork at the new museum honours Burramattagal man Daniel Moowattin, whose role collecting local plants for British botanist George Caley was largely erased from official records.
stories.detail: Bronze plaques carry eucalyptus clippings gathered on Dharug Country and research has recovered four Dharug words connected to eucalyptus species. The museum opens this Saturday, making this a timely Western Sydney visit from Epping as well as a piece of repaired local history.

stories.title: Apple largely removes the Siri AI waitlist
stories.summary: Apple has updated its support guidance so Siri AI begins downloading after a user selects Try Siri AI (Beta), instead of routinely placing them on a waitlist.
stories.detail: A waitlist can still appear during periods of high demand, so access is not guaranteed instantly. This is a server-side access change for eligible Siri AI users, not a new iOS release. The report does not establish any separate change to Australian device, language or regional eligibility.

stories.title: iOS 27.3 will check public iCloud links for harmful content
stories.summary: Apple says items shared using the Anyone with the Link option will be checked for harmful content in iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS 27.3 or later.
stories.detail: This applies to public links, not the People you choose sharing option. Apple says it may remove flagged material or act on an account. Version 27.3 is currently in beta, so this is announced behaviour rather than a general public release; no separate Australian rollout was specified.

stories.title: Tesla faces a South Korean complaint over unavailable FSD
stories.summary: A consumer group plans to ask South Korea's competition regulator to stop Tesla marketing Full Self-Driving (Supervised) to vehicles that cannot legally use it. Reuters reports only about 20 per cent of Teslas registered there are currently eligible.
stories.detail: The complaint alleges 99 per cent of new Teslas sold in South Korea last year were ineligible, mostly because China-built cars lacked certification. Tesla did not respond to Reuters. This has no confirmed effect on Australian Model Y owners, but it underlines how local certification and vehicle origin can determine availability. FSD remains supervised driver assistance, not autonomy.

stories.title: Google open-sources a method for defining AI's grey areas
stories.summary: Google Research has introduced Agile Deliberation, a framework that helps people iteratively define subjective categories and resolve edge cases before an AI image classifier is built.
stories.detail: In 18 live sessions, Google says the approach reduced fatigue and anxiety while producing more consistent classifiers than standard baselines. The code and algorithms are open source, but this is research rather than a Google Workspace product. Suggested work experiment: before automating customer-health or escalation labels, use an AI session to surface borderline examples and agree the rule with your team. That application is my suggestion, not a reported Google use case.

stories.title: Australians can now find Meta's hidden AI-training opt-out
stories.summary: ABC has confirmed Meta offers an objection form that lets Australian Facebook and Instagram users stop future public posts, photos and comments being used to train its AI, despite never announcing the option locally.
stories.detail: The form has existed since July 2025 but is buried in privacy settings. Meta says a successful submission triggers an email confirmation. Private accounts, private messages and accounts belonging to under-18s are already exempt. This affects future use, so it should not be read as deleting data already used in training.

stories.title: Canva restructure affects 22 per cent of its workforce
stories.summary: Canva says 1,270 jobs will be affected through cuts, changed roles or relocation as growth slows and new technology changes how customers create and use products.
stories.detail: Sydney will become the main product hub, with some staff asked to relocate and most hybrid employees expected in the office two or three days a week from January. Canva did not explicitly blame AI. The company says departing employees will receive at least six months' salary and other support.

stories.title: Democrats win both chambers in the US midterms
stories.summary: ABC's Associated Press results show Democrats have won the House and Senate, flipping seven Senate seats including Texas, Ohio and both Carolinas.
stories.detail: This is the substantive result after yesterday's voting, not a repeat of the election preview. Losing both chambers means President Donald Trump will need to negotiate with opponents to pass legislation during the rest of his term, with likely consequences for US trade, technology and foreign policy.

stories.title: The big four pass the full rate rise to mortgage customers
stories.summary: Commonwealth Bank, Westpac, NAB and ANZ will each lift variable home-loan rates by 0.25 percentage points after the RBA raised the cash rate to an 18-year high of 4.85 per cent.
stories.detail: This is the household-level follow-through from Tuesday's decision and the fifth cash-rate rise of 2026. Macquarie moved first and says its higher variable rates take effect on 19 November. Banks have also announced some savings-rate changes, though the pass-through and eligibility conditions vary.

stories.title: Education ministers move towards screen and AI limits in schools
stories.summary: Federal and state education ministers have agreed to consider school screen-time limits and restrictions on students using generative AI, with a new Australian Schools Digital Detox Taskforce to develop the details.
stories.detail: The announced direction includes restricting generative AI in primary schools and secondary-school assessments, but implementation settings still need to be worked through. NSW already has separate screen-time limits for public schools from next year, so the national work may extend or align existing state rules rather than replace them immediately.

editions.label: Wednesday, 4 November 2026
editions.note: Checked Wednesday morning, Sydney time. Stories are deduplicated by underlying event, with ABC and 9to5Mac preferred where coverage overlapped. Apple publication times were converted to Sydney time. Beta software, announced services, geographic limits and suggested applications are labelled explicitly.

stories.title: Housing sector proposes a 7.5 per cent levy on short stays
stories.summary: NSW's community housing peak body wants a new levy on Airbnb and Stayz bookings, alongside land-tax changes, to create a long-term funding pool for social and affordable homes.
stories.detail: The package could raise $26 billion over a decade and support about 50,000 homes by 2050, while the social housing waiting list has reached 72,000 households. These are industry proposals being presented to parliament today, not government policy.

stories.title: NSW Liberals face an MP exodus before the March election
stories.summary: Six Liberal MPs will not recontest next year's state election as the Coalition trails Labor and One Nation gains support, stripping the opposition of substantial experience.
stories.detail: Mark Coure is the third Liberal frontbencher in three months to announce his retirement. Optional preferential voting could let a split between Liberal and One Nation supporters help Labor in marginal seats such as Oatley. One Nation says it is recruiting across all 93 lower-house seats.

stories.title: iOS 27.3 beta opens advanced Siri app skills to developers
stories.summary: Apple's first iOS 27.3 developer beta lets third-party apps define multistep actions for Siri AI, while Apple has expanded Siri controls across Music, Messages, Notes, Photos, Calendar, Reminders, Files and more.
stories.detail: Developers can connect actions across apps and complete a task with one request. This is developer-beta software, not a public release, and support will depend on apps adopting the framework. Australian availability of every Siri AI capability is not confirmed.

stories.title: Apple's redesigned Health app returns in iOS 27.3 beta
stories.summary: The new Health app adds an Insights view across heart, sleep, readiness, fitness and vitals, plus a Longevity tab that estimates Health Age from Apple Watch data.
stories.detail: It also supports optional clinical lab data and at-home movement assessments using the iPhone camera and Apple Watch. Apple says analysis runs on-device without recording, storing or sharing video. A public release is expected next month, but the Australian date is unconfirmed.

stories.title: A SpaceX merger could reshape control of Tesla
stories.summary: Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a potential merger, and a Reuters analysis says the share structures could give Elon Musk majority voting control of a combined company.
stories.detail: Barclays estimates Musk could own about 37 per cent of the group but control 56 per cent of votes because some SpaceX shares carry extra voting power. This is analysis, not an announced transaction. There is no confirmed effect on Australia, Model Y owners or local services.

stories.title: Google brings Guided Learning into Classroom worldwide
stories.summary: Google has released Guided Learning globally in Google Classroom, where it coaches students through questions and step-by-step prompts instead of simply supplying answers.
stories.detail: A related Search feature begins as a pilot in selected US schools this month, so it is not generally available in Australia. Suggested work experiment: make a customer enablement prompt ask for the goal, evidence and next step before drafting a follow-up. That is a suggested adaptation, not a Google use case.

stories.title: European firms plan sovereign AI computing services
stories.summary: Schwarz Digits and French supercomputer maker Bull have signed a preliminary agreement to build AI computing services that operate entirely under European jurisdiction.
stories.detail: Schwarz would sell compute and storage through STACKIT, while Bull would manufacture servers and provide AI software. The plan reflects enterprise demand for data residency and local legal control. It is a preliminary agreement with no launch date, pricing or Australian availability.

stories.title: Fake job interview helped hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance
stories.summary: Binance says attackers compromised three software engineers through a tampered download, a malicious job-interview repository and stolen credentials before draining crypto from online wallets.
stories.detail: The intrusion culminated on 29 October, when 233.46 million XRP left five wallets in four minutes and transfers continued for almost four hours. The FBI blames a North Korean group, which Pyongyang rejects. Isolate interview exercises and verify repositories before running code on work devices.

stories.title: RBA lifts the cash rate to an 18-year high
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank raised the cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.85 per cent, its fifth increase of 2026, after concluding inflation will stay high for longer than expected.
stories.detail: The decision was split six votes to three. The RBA expects inflation to remain elevated through much of 2027 and not fall below 3 per cent until late that year. Borrowers face higher repayments if lenders pass the rise through, while savers may benefit.

stories.title: US voters decide control of Congress
stories.summary: Voting is under way in the US midterms, with Democrats narrow favourites to win both chambers and the result widely treated as a verdict on Donald Trump's presidency.
stories.detail: More than 50 million voted early. Cost-of-living pressure and fuel prices linked to the Iran war shaped the campaign. Polls had not begun closing at checking time, so forecasts are not results and close races may take days to settle.

stories.title: TGA clears Australia's first oral GLP-1 weight-loss drug
stories.summary: The Therapeutic Goods Administration has approved daily Wegovy tablets for people with obesity and those needing to reduce cardiovascular risk, making them Australia's first oral GLP-1 treatment.
stories.detail: Patients will need a prescription. The regulator must still review packaging and production before release, so approval does not mean immediate pharmacy availability. No Australian price is set, and current PBS rules subsidise weight-loss medicines only for people with type 2 diabetes.

stories.title: Ticketing tactics and expired flight credits earn Shonky Awards
stories.summary: Choice has named Ticketek, Ticketmaster and Virgin Australia among its 2026 Shonky Award recipients, criticising ticket pricing practices and $75 million in expired Virgin flight credits.
stories.detail: Choice cited John Farnham Tribute tickets priced up to $1,650 and NRL seats with a $50 premium. Ticketek says variable pricing affected less than 7 per cent of the tribute concert and excluded the $1,650 tickets. Virgin says more than 93 per cent of credits were redeemed.

editions.label: Tuesday, 3 November 2026
editions.note: Checked Tuesday morning, Sydney time. Stories are deduplicated by underlying event, with ABC and 9to5Mac preferred where coverage overlapped. Apple publication times were converted to Sydney time. Rumours, staged releases, availability limits and suggested applications are labelled explicitly.

stories.title: Western Sydney Airport noise fuels calls for a night curfew
stories.summary: Blue Mountains residents say aircraft noise has increased since Western Sydney International Airport opened to passengers on 25 October, and hundreds have backed a petition for an 11 pm to 6 am curfew.
stories.detail: Freight flights have operated around the clock since July, while passenger traffic is expected to grow as more airlines start services. Airservices Australia says daytime runway choices aim to minimise residential overflight where possible, but a UNSW aviation expert says every route involves trade-offs. The curfew campaign is new; no curfew has been announced.

stories.title: Hawkesbury Radio faces closure after eviction notice
stories.summary: Sydney Water has given the 48-year-old community station three months to leave its Windsor studios after an inspection found significant safety and compliance problems.
stories.detail: The volunteer-run station has streamed online since losing its FM licence in 2022 and says about 5,000 people listen each month. Locals relied on it during bushfires and floods, giving the threatened closure a public-safety dimension as well as a cultural one. Hawkesbury City Council is helping search for a new site, but says no suitable premises have yet been found.

stories.title: HomeView code points to a built-in HomeKit security camera
stories.summary: Code found in HomeView software 27.2 suggests Apple's new home display may support motion detection, live streaming and recording through HomeKit Secure Video.
stories.detail: The settings reportedly include separate controls for when people are home, away or asleep, plus an indicator light, an audible start signal and household notifications. Remote activation may be blocked while anyone is home. Apple has not announced the feature, so availability at launch, including in Australia, is unconfirmed.

stories.title: Affinity brings its all-in-one design app to iPad
stories.summary: Canva has released Affinity for iPad, combining sketching, vector, photo and page-layout tools in one touch-first app that is free for individual users.
stories.detail: It supports Apple Pencil features including pressure, tilt, hover, squeeze and barrel roll, while projects can move from rough sketch to print-ready file without changing apps. This is an actual release rather than a preview. The App Store listing is live, although 9to5Mac did not separately confirm Australian regional availability.

stories.title: Tesla plans a layout fix for Android foldables
stories.summary: Tesla's new large-screen app can remain stuck in a stretched phone layout on some foldables until the device is rotated, and a company UI engineer says screen-size breakpoints will be refined in a future release.
stories.detail: The acknowledgement is useful but not a shipped fix, and Tesla has not provided a version or date. It affects the phone app rather than the car, so there is no Model Y hardware requirement. The workaround is to rotate an unfolded device to landscape; Australian availability of the eventual update has not been confirmed.

stories.title: A new Tesla factory build appears, without public release notes
stories.summary: Release tracking recorded software 2026.32.300 on 2 November, but no feature list or wider fleet rollout was available at checking time.
stories.detail: The .300 numbering normally indicates factory-installed software, so it should not be treated as an owner update. There is no confirmed Australian distribution, Model Y applicability or action to take. No more significant Tesla vehicle, autonomy, charging, energy, robotics or regulatory development was verified inside the 24-hour window.
stories.source: Not a Tesla App release tracker

stories.title: ADNOC plans connected AI agents across its energy business
stories.summary: ADNOC, OpenAI and G42 have announced a multi-year deployment that will connect operational, capital and commercial decisions using GPT models on UAE-based infrastructure.
stories.detail: The first uses are field planning across decades of well and facility data, and coordinating production, refining, logistics, sales and trading. Human experts will retain oversight of consequential decisions. Suggested Braze application: build a meeting-prep workflow that joins CRM notes, the last transcript and open actions, but requires citations and human approval before drafting follow-ups. That is a suggested adaptation, not a reported ADNOC use case.

stories.title: Hidden deepfake network slipped through mobile app reviews
stories.summary: An investigation found more than 400 connected apps and domains that could activate sexual and violent deepfake tools after presenting benign functions during review.
stories.detail: The apps appeared in both Apple's App Store and Google Play, while advertising also ran on Meta platforms. Apple said developers changed remotely loaded web content after approval and removed 19 apps after being notified; Meta said it acted against more than 10,000 linked ad accounts. The episode shows how server-side behaviour can bypass one-off review checks.

stories.title: Hackers turn up supermarket fridge temperatures across Europe
stories.summary: Grocery stores in at least seven European countries reported refrigeration failures, with several confirming a cyberattack that forced chilled and frozen food to be discarded.
stories.detail: Affected chains included Carrefour, Coop, Delhaize and ICA, with some systems reportedly set as high as 50 degrees Celsius. Investigators have not attributed the attack. The practical lesson is broader than retail: remotely managed operational devices need current patches, network isolation and independent monitoring because a small control compromise can create immediate physical losses.

stories.title: RBA is widely expected to lift rates this afternoon
stories.summary: Economists and markets expect the Reserve Bank to raise the cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.85 per cent at 2:30 pm AEDT, which would be an 18-year high.
stories.detail: That would be the fifth increase this year after inflation stayed above target. The result is not yet known, so this is a decision-day preview rather than a confirmed hike. Michele Bullock is due to speak at 3:30 pm, when borrowers will get clearer guidance on whether the Bank still sees more tightening ahead.

stories.title: Trump's red-state campaign trail signals Republican nerves
stories.summary: Donald Trump has concentrated late campaigning in normally safe Republican states as US voters head to the midterms, with analysts reading the itinerary as a defensive push to protect the Senate.
stories.detail: Texas and Kansas are among the unexpectedly close Senate contests, while Democrats are favoured in many House races. Polls close over the coming Australian day, and no result should be inferred yet. Control of either chamber would shape the final two years of Trump's term and US policy on spending, trade and foreign affairs.

editions.label: Monday, 2 November 2026
editions.note: Checked Monday morning, Sydney time. Stories are deduplicated by underlying event, with ABC preferred where coverage overlapped. Apple publication times were converted to Sydney time. Rumours, staged releases, availability limits and suggested applications are labelled explicitly.

stories.title: NSW begins its 12-month gun buyback
stories.summary: Licensed owners can start surrendering firearms for payment today as NSW and the ACT become the first jurisdictions to join the national buyback announced after the Bondi terrorist attack.
stories.detail: The first phase is voluntary, with appointments initially available at six police stations including Penrith, Sutherland and Narellan. Another 34 stations are due to join in early December. Payments range from $450 to $1,000 in phase one, while regulations covering ownership caps and possible exemptions are still being finalised.

stories.title: NSW seeks a return to handwritten NAPLAN writing tests
stories.summary: NSW will ask education ministers today to move year 5, 7 and 9 NAPLAN writing tests from computers back to pen and paper from 2028.
stories.detail: Experts cited research linking handwriting with learning and memory, and said students should generally be tested in the same medium they use in class. The proposal needs national agreement and would require accommodations for students with additional needs. Marking costs and the limited teaching of keyboard skills are likely to be part of the debate.

stories.title: Rumour points to three iPad updates in early 2027
stories.summary: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reportedly expects refreshed iPad Air, iPad Pro and entry-level iPad models in the first half of 2027.
stories.detail: The report says the Air could gain OLED, the Pro may add vapour-chamber cooling, and the base iPad could move to an A19 chip with Apple Intelligence support. None of this has been announced by Apple, and Australian timing or pricing is unknown. This was the only substantive Apple hardware report found inside the 24-hour window, so the section stays short.

stories.title: Small Tesla rollout adds collision evasion and home backup features
stories.summary: Release tracker data shows software 2026.27.11 reaching about 0.21 per cent of cars, with FSD v14.3.10, Automatic Collision Evasion and vehicle-to-home support among the listed changes.
stories.detail: This is a very limited staged rollout observed in the US, Canada and Lithuania, not a broad global release. Some Model Y variants with HW4 and Ryzen hardware appear eligible, but vehicle-to-home also requires compatible charging equipment and Powerwall. Australian availability and applicability to your particular Model Y are not confirmed, so there is nothing to install or change yet.

stories.title: Major AI release desks were quiet overnight
stories.summary: Checks of official model and product logs found no significant new general-purpose AI model or workplace feature released in the previous 24 hours.
stories.detail: The latest OpenAI model entry remains its 30 October limited GPT-6 Rosalind Research rollout, which is restricted to approved life-sciences research customers and is not a general workplace tool. Suggested use for the quiet window: tighten one customer follow-up workflow by requiring transcript citations, an explicit confidence check and human approval before any draft is sent.

stories.title: AI is raising the stakes for attacks on critical infrastructure
stories.summary: Australian security specialists warn that AI can accelerate the discovery and exploitation of weaknesses in operational technology used across water, energy, transport and other essential services.
stories.detail: The report revisits Australia's 2000 Maroochy sewage attack as an early operational-technology case and notes the ASD's warning that critical systems attract state actors, criminals and hacktivists. For customer success automation, the practical lesson is to treat uploaded files and copied web content as untrusted, restrict tool permissions, and keep approval gates around any action that changes customer data.

stories.title: Meta reportedly builds a humanoid prototype with Fourier
stories.summary: Meta has reportedly built a 48-kilogram humanoid prototype with Chinese robotics company Fourier and started work on a second version with improved hands and stair-climbing sensors.
stories.detail: The prototype, called Max internally, is said to use Nvidia's Jetson Thor chip and to be designed for voice, gesture and household interaction research. Meta told the original reporter the units are for internal experimentation and are not planned for sale. The report has not been independently verified, so it is evidence of research progress rather than a product announcement.

stories.title: Australian housing downturn nears a 40-year record
stories.summary: National home values fell 1.2 per cent in October, the seventh consecutive monthly decline, leaving the median dwelling about $63,400 below its March peak.
stories.detail: Cotality says capital-city values are down 8.1 per cent in seven months, close to exceeding the 8.2 per cent fall recorded in the previous worst downturn from 2017 to 2019. Higher interest rates have cut borrowing capacity and sales volumes are sharply lower. That matters directly to Sydney owners and buyers, even though conditions vary by suburb.

stories.title: Iran and Qatari mediators continue talks to end the war
stories.summary: Iranian negotiators and Qatari mediators have entered a third day of talks in Doha over a possible path out of the eight-month US-Israeli war on Iran.
stories.detail: Iran says consultations are progressing but no final decision has been reached. A proposal under discussion could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days of an agreement, easing pressure on oil shipping and prices. The diplomacy is fragile, with Tehran maintaining military readiness and the US leaving open the possibility of further strikes after the midterm elections.

stories.title: Former US officials warn of presidential interference in midterms
stories.summary: Former CIA and FBI chiefs and past Trump administration advisers say the president's attacks on the electoral process could foreshadow interference before, during or after this week's vote.
stories.detail: Concerns include possible federal immigration officers at polling places and legal efforts to obstruct certification. Polling suggests Democrats could win the House and may take the Senate, turning the contest into a major test of Trump's second term. The claims are warnings from former officials, not evidence that interference has already occurred.
